gender.label: female
gender.evidence: if you’re a woman then you’ve more than likely got the – you’ve got to do the family thing
gender.reasoning: Subject refers to herself as a woman; interview is of women engineering students.

school.label: Mixed sex
school.evidence: No, no, mixed sort of schooling then over 2 erm, we didn’t have a sixth form
school.reasoning: Explicitly attended a mixed comprehensive school.

dept.label: Aeronautical & Automotive Engineering
dept.evidence: even in something as specialist as aeronautical engineering, you’re looking at everything related to aircraft

mathsci.label: Strongly agree
mathsci.evidence: I always really enjoyed maths at school and it was something that out of all the subjects, it was something I could do – that and physics … I was quite good at it
mathsci.reasoning: Strongly and repeatedly affirms being good at maths and physics at school.

varied.label: Strongly agree
varied.evidence: I’ll do aeronautical engineering because it kind of combines everything … you study such a vast range of modules you sort of – it’s a bit of everything … Something to keep you interested
varied.reasoning: Variety is the named main appeal of choosing engineering; emphatic 'Absolutely'.

special.label: agree
special.evidence: if you do sort of maths and physics, it’s just a bit hard core really … whereas with engineering you study such a vast range of modules
special.reasoning: Chose engineering to use maths/physics without specialising in either alone.

interest.label: Strongly agree
interest.evidence: Something to keep you interested. If you were just doing physics, I mean you’d just get really bored with it, so that’s why I chose it
interest.reasoning: Chose engineering for interesting work over a 'boring' single subject.

knowledg.label: agree
knowledg.evidence: before I came, I really didn’t – I wasn’t that clued about what engineering was about … But I’ve got to be honest, I didn’t really know what it entailed when I came here
knowledg.reasoning: Explicitly chose with little knowledge of what engineers actually do.

family.label: strongly disagree
family.evidence: No er none of them did anything like maths or physics or anything – it’s completely unrelated. My dad’s in – he sort of coaches and my mum works in [retail store]
family.reasoning: No family member in the industry at the time of choosing the degree.

careers.label: Strongly agree
careers.evidence: he was really good actually. He said, you know, if you did go to University, looking at the subjects you do, you’d probably want to do aeronautical engineering
careers.reasoning: Sixth-form careers advisor actively steered her to aeronautical engineering; 'Quite supportive' affirmed.

discoura.label: no
discoura.evidence: no, I don’t think I received any discouragement from anyone

placemen.label: no
placemen.evidence: I don’t believe I need t o take an entire year out just to have this diploma in industry on my CV
placemen.reasoning: Not going on placement; declined the year out.

wkexp.label: Strongly agree
wkexp.evidence: I’ve already had a year out in industry, so I’ve been in the real world, I know what it’s about … I’ve been in part time work since I was 13, I don’t really feel the need to spend another year out of my education, working
wkexp.reasoning: Primary stated reason for not going: already has work experience.

nogain.label: agree
nogain.evidence: other than that I can’t really think of anything that would benefit me personally
nogain.reasoning: Sees nothing to be gained personally from a placement (though notes others would benefit).

jobprosp.label: disagree
jobprosp.evidence: it’s an entire year, which is a long time to improve my employability by a tiny bit really
jobprosp.reasoning: Rejects placement as a route to better job prospects; sees only a tiny employability gain.

carpath.label: don't know
carpath.evidence: if you wanted to sort of look at air flows and wings and stuff or if you wanted to design fuselages or whatever, that kind of thing
carpath.reasoning: Leans toward hands-on aerodynamic/design work over management, though uncertain which specialism.

alt.label: do not want career in engineering
alt.evidence: I’m interested in engineering but it’s not what I want my career – I don’t want to make my career out of it, I just want to get the money

workrole.label: technical/specialist
workrole.evidence: I’d much rather be on the shop floor with everyone doing the engineering thing
workrole.reasoning: Prefers technical/specialist hands-on role over managerial paperwork.

salary.label: very important
salary.evidence: it would be what areas they specialise in, erm location, salary, salary (laughter) – that’s quite a big pull
salary.reasoning: Repeats 'salary, salary' as a big pull when choosing a job.

location.label: important
location.evidence: it would be what areas they specialise in, erm location, salary
location.reasoning: Lists location among the things that would attract her to a company.

training.label: unimportant
training.evidence: no, not so much training opportunities, that wouldn’t really bother me because I think I’ve had you know, I’ve learnt a lot here
training.reasoning: Explicitly says training opportunities would not really bother/attract her.

equalopp.label: unimportant
equalopp.evidence: I think Equal Opportunities are getting less and less of an issue these days – personally … it wouldn’t really attract me to a company
equalopp.reasoning: States equal-opportunities policies would not attract her to a company.

people.label: important
people.evidence: The worst thing would be not having many people in a common position that you can go to … I guess loneliness really is how you could describe it
people.reasoning: Strongly values having peers/people in a common position; bigger company attraction confirmed.

pleased.label: Strongly agree
pleased.evidence: No, I don’t think I would. Yeah, I ‘m quite happy I mean I don’t regret anything … I don’t see it as a drawback at all
pleased.reasoning: Happy with her choices, no regrets, would not change anything.

curricul.label: disagree
curricul.evidence: it’s hard – it’s hard work, which I knew it would be hard work and it’s very hour intensive
curricul.reasoning: Course is very hard/hour-intensive; though she also says it matched expectations, supports difficulty.

variety.label: very satisfied
variety.evidence: how varied it is and in every single module it’s really difficult
variety.reasoning: Consistently positive about the breadth/variety of subjects; variety is her chief draw.

friends.label: very satisfied
friends.evidence: the best things is – I don’t know, the people you meet. They’re all kind of like minded … it’s a really nice kind of spirit amongst everyone
friends.reasoning: People/friends on the course are named the best thing; warm peer spirit.

interper.label: Strongly agree
interper.evidence: it’s developed me as a person, it’s helped my communication skills and that kind of thing

groupwk.label: satisfied
groupwk.evidence: it sort of develops, your sort of listening skills and communication skills and that sort of thing. I think it’s essential
groupwk.reasoning: Views group work positively and as essential preparation for industry.
